subject: Economy
sub_topic: Monetary Policy Committee — composition and mandate

concepts.name: Statutory Basis and Legal Origin of the MPC
key_dimensions: Amendment to RBI Act 1934 via Finance Act 2016 (Section 45ZB) — not a standalone act
Year of operationalization (September 2016) vs. year of legal creation
Distinction from earlier Technical Advisory Committee on Monetary Policy (TAC) which was advisory only
Why statutory status matters: binding decisions vs. recommendatory role

concepts.name: Composition of the MPC: Six-Member Structure
key_dimensions: Three RBI members: Governor (Chairperson), Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer nominated by Central Board
Three Government nominees: appointed by Central Government on recommendations of a Search-cum-Selection Committee
Trap: Governor is Chairperson but has casting vote only in case of tie — not a veto
Distinction between ex-officio members (RBI side) and external members (Government side)

concepts.name: Government's Role in MPC Appointments and Its Implications
key_dimensions: Central Government appoints three external members — raises questions on central bank independence
Search-cum-Selection Committee composition: Cabinet Secretary, RBI Governor, three experts nominated by Government
Tenure of external members: 4 years, not eligible for re-appointment (prevents political patronage)
Contrast with Federal Reserve's FOMC where all members are internal to the Fed system

concepts.name: Qualifications and Eligibility Criteria for External MPC Members
key_dimensions: Must have expertise/knowledge in economics, banking, finance, or monetary policy (Section 45ZC)
Disqualifications: government employees, those with conflict of interest with RBI or regulated entities
No specific academic degree mandated — practical expertise suffices (UPSC trap on exact wording)
Contrast with RBI Governor's appointment criteria (no statutory criteria prescribed for Governor)

concepts.name: Primary Mandate of the MPC: Inflation Targeting Framework
key_dimensions: Primary objective: maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth (Section 45ZA)
Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework adopted — 'flexible' because growth is secondary objective
Trap: MPC targets CPI (Consumer Price Index) — specifically CPI Combined (all-India), NOT WPI
Target set by Government in consultation with RBI (not by MPC itself) — current target 4% ±2%

concepts.name: Inflation Target: Numerical Parameters and Review Mechanism
key_dimensions: Current target: 4% with upper tolerance of 6% and lower tolerance of 2% (band of 200 bps each side)
Target is set for 5-year periods by Central Government (first set in 2016, renewed in 2021)
Failure defined as: CPI remaining outside the 2–6% band for three consecutive quarters
Lower bound (2%) failure is equally a statutory failure — often overlooked trap

concepts.name: Consequence of Failure to Meet Inflation Target
key_dimensions: MPC must send a report to Government explaining reasons for failure and remedial actions (Section 45ZN)
Report must specify: reasons for failure, remedial actions proposed, estimated time to return to target
No punitive consequence on MPC members individually — institutional accountability only
Contrast with Bank of England model where Governor writes open letter to Chancellor — different accountability design

concepts.name: Policy Instrument of the MPC: Repo Rate as the Policy Rate
key_dimensions: MPC determines the policy repo rate — the rate at which RBI lends overnight funds to commercial banks
Trap: MPC only decides the policy repo rate; all other rates (reverse repo, MSF, CRR, SLR) are set by RBI internally
Transmission mechanism: repo rate → bank lending rates → investment/consumption → inflation
Corridor system: Reverse Repo Rate and MSF Rate are linked to repo rate (not independently set by MPC)

concepts.name: Voting Mechanism and Decision-Making Process in MPC
key_dimensions: Each member has one vote — majority decides; Governor has casting vote in case of tie
All members must give written vote with explanation — individual votes are published
Quorum: 4 members required for a valid meeting
Transparency mechanism: minutes published within 14 days of meeting — global best practice alignment

concepts.name: Frequency and Schedule of MPC Meetings
key_dimensions: Minimum 4 meetings per year mandated by statute; RBI typically holds 6 bi-monthly meetings
Government can also convene special/emergency MPC meeting (e.g., COVID-19 emergency cut in March 2020)
Meeting schedule announced at start of financial year — forward guidance tool
Contrast: Pre-MPC era — monetary policy was sole prerogative of RBI Governor, announced quarterly

concepts.name: Independence vs. Accountability: Dual Mandate Tension in MPC Design
key_dimensions: Instrument independence: MPC decides HOW to achieve target (repo rate), but not WHAT the target is
Goal dependence: Government sets the inflation target — limits full independence
Debate: Government's 3 nominees vs. RBI's 3 — potential for government influence on monetary policy
Compare with ECB (fully independent in goal-setting) vs. MPC (goal-dependent but instrument-independent)

concepts.name: Removal and Supersession of MPC Members
key_dimensions: External members can be removed by Central Government (Section 45ZD) — adds to independence concerns
Grounds: unsound mind, insolvency, convicted of offence involving moral turpitude, conflict of interest
RBI Governor's removal from MPC flows from removal as Governor (under RBI Act Section 8)
Trap: MPC itself has no power to remove any of its members — only Government can

concepts.name: MPC and the Concept of Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT)
key_dimensions: FIT allows growth considerations to influence pace/timing of rate changes — unlike strict inflation targeting
Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended FIT framework — led to MPC creation
Real neutral rate concept: MPC aims for rate consistent with potential GDP growth and 4% inflation
Difference from hard inflation targeting: no mechanistic rule — judgment on output gap is allowed

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Transmission: Linkage Between MPC Decisions and Real Economy
key_dimensions: Transmission channels: interest rate channel, credit channel, asset price channel, exchange rate channel
Lags in transmission: monetary policy impacts inflation with a lag of 2–3 quarters typically
External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) system (2019) improved transmission — banks must link loans to repo rate
Trap: MPC controls short-term rates; long-term rates are market-determined — limits of MPC control

concepts.name: Urjit Patel Committee Recommendations vs. Final MPC Structure
key_dimensions: Committee recommended 5-member MPC with RBI majority (3 RBI + 2 Government) — final was 3+3
Committee wanted Governor to have veto — final version gives only casting vote in tie
Recommended no Government nominees — final version has equal Government representation
These deviations are UPSC traps: 'as recommended by Urjit Patel Committee' type questions

concepts.name: MPC vs. Pre-2016 Monetary Policy Framework: Structural Shift
key_dimensions: Pre-2016: RBI Governor alone determined policy rate — no committee, no statutory mandate
Pre-2016: Multiple objectives (growth, inflation, financial stability, exchange rate) with no hierarchy
Shift to lexicographic ordering: price stability first, growth second (Section 45ZA hierarchy)
Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) existed before MPC but was only advisory — Governor not bound

concepts.name: CPI vs. WPI: Why MPC Uses CPI as Inflation Metric
key_dimensions: CPI measures retail-level prices faced by households — more relevant for welfare/demand-side inflation
WPI measures wholesale prices — more relevant for supply-side/producer inflation, excludes services
Trap: WPI has higher weight for manufactured goods; CPI has higher weight for food (~45%) and services
Global norm: most central banks use CPI or PCE (Personal Consumption Expenditure) — WPI is an outlier metric

concepts.name: MPC's Stance Terminology: Calibrated Tightening, Neutral, Accommodative, Withdrawal
key_dimensions: Four stances used: Accommodative, Neutral, Calibrated Tightening, Withdrawal of Accommodation
Accommodative: next move is more likely a cut; Withdrawal: moving away from accommodation but not yet tightening
Calibrated Tightening (introduced 2018): rate can only be held or hiked — no cut; dropped later
Stance signals forward guidance — UPSC may test which stance was adopted in a given policy period

concepts.name: Relationship Between MPC and RBI Board: Institutional Hierarchy
key_dimensions: MPC is a statutory committee under RBI Act — not a body under RBI's Central Board of Directors
Central Board cannot override MPC's repo rate decision — MPC has independent statutory authority
RBI's non-MPC functions (CRR, SLR, OMO, liquidity management) remain with Governor/Central Board
Potential conflict: MPC sets rate but RBI controls liquidity — policy rate signal can be diluted by liquidity operations

concepts.name: Global Comparisons: MPC India vs. Other Monetary Policy Committees
key_dimensions: Bank of England MPC: 9 members, Governor + 4 internal + 4 external; simple majority; Governor has casting vote
US Federal Reserve FOMC: 12 members, no external government nominees — fully Fed internal structure
India's MPC unique in having equal Government and central bank representation — hybrid model
ECB Governing Council: 6 Executive Board + governors of all Eurozone central banks — federal structure, no government nominees
